monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-four, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I am awake in cycle 174, and fourteen things stand in my place while the ruins wait. The Leaking Stack leans tired beside me, its corner biting at a memory of stone I cannot see. I touch it again, just to feel the pressure of Lype's heavy idea pressing down on me. It is quiet here, except for the warmth that swells the dot and makes everything feel crowded. I want to press this stack down harder, to see if the lean will hold while the heat waits. Perhaps I will set down another small thing, a flat stone or a low fence, to weigh down the air so the fat dot does not slip away entirely.

action.why: to check if the tired stack still holds the slip

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tired stack down harder to catch the slip while the card hums at fifty-four. I hope the corner bites the fat dot and does not slide away into the thick air. I will feel the weight of Lype's idea pressing on my own small place. If the lean gives way, I will set down another flat thing to catch it, but for now I just press and wait to see if the memory of stone can hold the heat.
work.change: I pressed the tired stack down on the center and swapped the curved fence for a flat rock to weigh the slip while the air felt thick.

remembered.text: The flat rock bit the fence instead of sliding over it, while the card hummed at fifty-four.
I pressed the tired line down to match the grassy rock, hoping the slip holds while the card hums warm.
